source_text:
CYR.Περὶ τούτων τῶν κεφαλαίων μακρὸς ἡμῖν πεποίηται λόγος, ὅτε
ἐγράφομεν εἰς τὸν
 Ὠσηὲ τὸν προφήτην, καὶ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ δὲ τῷ περὶ τῆς Γενέσεως
πολλὴ βάσανος εὑρίσκεται περὶ τοῦ Μελχισεδέκ, καὶ ἔξεστι τῇ εὐλαβείᾳ σου ταῖς
βίβλοις ἐντυχεῖν κἀκεῖθεν λαβεῖν τῶν εἰρημένων ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τὸν νοῦν.

Επιτρέπεται η ελεύθερη χρήση του υλικού µε αναφορά στην πηγή προέλευσής του.

1
thought_title: Where to find fuller discussion of these questions
orientation: Cyril is closing the fragment by pointing his reader to his earlier, longer treatments of Hosea and Melchizedek.
pass_a_gloss: About these headings a long account has been made by us, when we were writing on Hosea the prophet, and in the book about Genesis much examination is found about Melchizedek, and it is possible for your reverence to meet with the books and from there to take the sense of the things said on each point.

choices.why: The word refers to the main questions or topics just raised, not to chapters of a book.

choices.english: a long account has been made by us
choices.why: The perfect passive with dative of agent keeps the emphasis on the completed written discussion.
rejected: we have made a long discourse
a long word has been made for us

choices.why: The term means a testing or close scrutiny, fitting a detailed treatment of Melchizedek.

choices.english: it is possible for your reverence
choices.why: The impersonal verb with dative preserves the polite address to the reader.
The verb means to encounter or read a text, not merely to have access to it.

choices.term: τῶν εἰρημένων ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τὸν νοῦν
choices.english: the sense of the things said on each point
choices.why: The genitive with νοῦν and the distributive ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ preserves the idea of the meaning for each topic.
rejected: the mind of what has been said on each
the understanding of each thing said

pass_b_english: I have already written at length about these questions in my commentary on the prophet Hosea, and in the book on Genesis you will find a thorough examination of Melchizedek. Your reverence can read those books and take from them the meaning of what has been said on each point.

problems.quote: take from them the meaning of what has been said
problems.why: 'Take from them the meaning' is awkward; should be 'learn the meaning'
problems.fix: Read 'find the meaning' or 'learn the interpretation'

edits.old: take from them the meaning of what has been said
edits.new: learn from them the meaning of what has been said

problems.why: Ambiguous whether this is a commentary title or generic reference

fixed: Changed 'the book on Genesis' to 'my work On Genesis' to clarify that this refers to Cyril's own treatise on Genesis, matching the source's 'ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ δὲ τῷ περὶ τῆς Γενέσεως' in context.
